simple.meaning: יָסַךְ (yâçak) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to pour (intransitive).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Exodus, beginning at Exodus 30:32. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָסַךְ (H3251) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָסַךְ (yâçak) / H3251 is traced through Exodus 30:32 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: It shall not be poured on man’s flesh, and do not make any like it, according to its composition. It is holy. It shall be holy to you.
